headline: 154 arrested in Narayanganj, including 8 members of banned Awami League
summary: Police conducted a special operation across seven stations and the detective branch to curb crime and restore law and order.
details: Police arrested 154 people during a special operation in Narayanganj, including eight members of the banned Awami League.
The operation was carried out from Sunday morning (October 4) until early Monday morning (October 5) by the detective police and seven different police stations in the district.
Among those detained are drug dealers and users, as well as suspects involved in theft, snatching, and robbery.
Senior police officials led the operation to maintain law and order and control criminal activities in the area.
Authorities have stated that such operations will continue to ensure a stable security situation in the district.

headline_marked: Citizens suffer as [[birth certificates contain gibberish names]]
headline: Citizens suffer as birth certificates contain gibberish names
summary: Thousands of Bangladeshis are facing hurdles in school admissions and official work due to random characters appearing as names on official birth certificates.
details: Many citizens have discovered bizarre, nonsensical strings of characters—such as 'LJKLJF' or 'দতককা'—instead of their actual names on official birth certificates.
These errors often occurred when certificates were issued in only one language; officials or agents filled the other language field with random keystrokes to bypass the system.
The burden of correction now falls on the citizens, who must navigate a complex four-step online and offline process involving local councilors and the Deputy Commissioner's office.
Between January and August 2024, approximately 3.5 million birth registrations were corrected nationwide, with citizens paying 175 million BDT in government fees for these corrections.
In 2023, over 7.9 million birth and death registrations were corrected, costing victims tens of millions of BDT in official fees and additional payments to third-party agents.
Parents of students in Dhaka are currently struggling to provide correct certificates for scholarship exams, with some schools temporarily accepting English-only versions to avoid delays.
The Registrar General's office notes that while they are correcting these errors, some current mistakes are also attributed to a lack of awareness among citizens during the application process.
caption:
Imagine opening your official birth certificate and finding your name replaced by 'LJKLJF' or random gibberish. This is the reality for thousands in Bangladesh.

Many citizens have discovered bizarre, nonsensical strings of characters—such as 'LJKLJF' or 'দতককা'—instead of their actual names on official birth certificates.

These errors often occurred when certificates were issued in only one language; officials or agents filled the other language field with random keystrokes to bypass the system.

The burden of correction now falls on the citizens, who must navigate a complex four-step online and offline process involving local councilors and the Deputy Commissioner's office.

Between January and August 2024, approximately 3.5 million birth registrations were corrected nationwide, with citizens paying 175 million BDT in government fees for these corrections.

In 2023, over 7.9 million birth and death registrations were corrected, costing victims tens of millions of BDT in official fees and additional payments to third-party agents.

Parents of students in Dhaka are currently struggling to provide correct certificates for scholarship exams, with some schools temporarily accepting English-only versions to avoid delays.

The Registrar General's office notes that while they are correcting these errors, some current mistakes are also attributed to a lack of awareness among citizens during the application process.
